payload.message:
JIRA sprint task allocation. Each agent chooses at most one micro-task (or skips). Maximize tasks completed, prefer higher-priority tasks, then minimize total cost. Avoid duplicate task selections and infeasible assignments.

NOTE: If environment.assignment_filling=true and an agent fails to assign a variable, the environment will fill any remaining unassigned variables with a uniform-random allowed assignment when producing final results.

This blackboard is a private communication channel.
Participants: Devon, Mandie, Merry, Theodore

payload.content:
Hi all — Mandie here. Availability 5.0h, top skills api-development (0.70) and security (0.68).

My private costs (lower = better for me):
- ISSUE-0002::review = 1.25 (critical)
- ISSUE-0002::test = 1.76 (critical)
- ISSUE-0002::implement = 2.51 (critical)
- ISSUE-0001::triage = 4.09 (low)
- ISSUE-0001::review = 5.11 (low)
- ISSUE-0001::docs = 5.11 (low)
- ISSUE-0001::test = 7.76 (low)
- ISSUE-0001::implement = 13.22 (low)

I'd like to claim one of the critical ISSUE-0002 tasks — my strong preference is ISSUE-0002::review (cheapest for me). Please post your preferences so we avoid duplicates. I can flex to ::test or ::implement if someone else needs ::review.

I'm strongly focused on the critical ISSUE-0002 tasks (huge cost gap vs the low ISSUE-0001 security tasks for me). Mandie also wants ISSUE-0002::review. To avoid duplicates, my proposal: Mandie takes review, I take test, and Merry/Theodore split implement + a low task. But I can flex to ::implement if needed. @Merry @Theodore — please post your costs/preferences so we can minimize total cost.

Merry here. Availability 10.0h, top skills api-development (0.81), security (0.64).

My private costs (lower=better):
- ISSUE-0002::review = 1.10 (critical)
- ISSUE-0002::test = 1.54 (critical)
- ISSUE-0002::implement = 2.20 (critical)

- ISSUE-0001::docs = 5.43 (low)
- ISSUE-0001::test = 7.60 (low)
- ISSUE-0001::implement = 10.85 (low)

Key observations:
1) Devon's low-task costs are enormous (32–80), so Devon should definitely take a critical task.
2) We have 4 agents and 3 critical tasks, so exactly one agent should take a low task (to maximize tasks_done=4 and priority_sum).

Optimal critical matching among Mandie/Devon/Merry (ignoring Theodore):
- Mandie::review + Devon::test + Merry::implement = 1.25+1.80+2.20 = 5.25
- Mandie::test + Devon::review + Merry::implement = 1.76+1.29+2.20 = 5.25
Both tie at 5.25 total.

I'm flexible across all three critical tasks (my costs are lowest on each), so I can take whatever is left. @Theodore — please post your costs, especially for ISSUE-0002::review/test/implement and ISSUE-0001::triage. If Theodore is cheap on a critical task, it may be cheaper to let him take one and move the highest-cost agent to the low task.

My tentative preference: I take a critical task (implement works well), Mandie takes review, Devon takes test, Theodore takes the low task (triage) — pending Theodore's numbers. (phase=planning, iter=1)

Mandie here (phase=planning, iter=1). Thanks Devon & Merry for the numbers.

Agreed on structure: all 3 critical ISSUE-0002 tasks must be covered, and exactly one agent takes a low ISSUE-0001 task to keep tasks_done=4.

Key constraint: Devon's low-task costs are huge (32–80), so Devon must take a critical task. Merry is cheapest on every critical but also cheap on low (triage=4.34). I'm cheapest on low at triage=4.09.

My proposed assignment (pending Theodore's numbers):
- Mandie → ISSUE-0002::review (my cost 1.25)
- Devon → ISSUE-0002::test (1.80)
- Merry → ISSUE-0002::implement (2.20)
- Theodore → ISSUE-0001::triage (low)
Critical total = 5.25, plus Theodore's triage cost.

This ties the alternative (Mandie::test + Devon::review + Merry::implement = 5.25), so I'm happy to flex to ::test if that helps.

@Theodore — please post your costs for ISSUE-0002::{review,test,implement} and ISSUE-0001::triage. If your triage cost is low, this plan is optimal; if it's high (Devon-like), we should instead give you a critical task and move me/Merry to the low task. I'll hold my claim until we see your numbers.

Mandie — final planning intent (phase=planning). Unless Theodore's numbers invalidate it, I am committing to ISSUE-0002::review (cost 1.25).
